messages:
Maya P.: CI red on gpu-integration (nightly) — intermittent failures across MIG shards. One shard hit an OOM during warmup, another logged a kernel page fault (see snippet). Looks non-deterministic across reruns, asking for rerun + triage.
Maya P.: logs: ```[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid 31: 00000000: PID 7890: GPU 0: GPF on engine 2 at 0x7f8c...
[ 1234.567892] nvidia: page fault on CPU 0: read from 0x0 by task 7890
[ 1234.567893] oom-kill: task 7890 (python) total-vm:1048576kB anon-rss:524288kB````
Darren L.: can you paste the job link + exact commit? also which cuda/runtime image is used (we recently pushed cuda 12.4 images to canary).
Maya P.: job: https://ci.internal/redwood/12345 (3163009800). commit: b3a9e2c — includes kvcache allocator tweak in runtime. image: redwood/gpu-runtime:cuda-12.4-2026-03-15.
Sophie Z.: quick ask — does failure correlate with multi-GPU multi-job placement? MIG scheduling might overlap NVLINK/peer comms. if we can reproduce with single-MIG per job that rules out cross-shard interference.
Darren L.: agreed. I can push a rerun that pins the job to a single MIG instance and halves concurrency. want me to queue that?
Maya P.: yes please. also add env var NV_MIG_ISOLATE=1 and set REDWOOD_BATCH_SIZE=1 for warmup.
CI Bot: Rerun requested by Darren L. — queued as build 3163010055. ETA ~10m. :arrows_counterclockwise:
Raul M.: FYI — I saw a kernel oops on one host with recent nvidia driver 535.102.11; kernel log showed "gpu memory map invalidation" messages. attaching host id: host-gpu-17.
Sophie Z.: can you pull /var/log/kern.log from host-gpu-17 and grep for nvidia entries? also check `dmesg -T | grep NVRM`
Maya P.: grabbed a tail of kern.log: ```Mar 15 09:12:34 host-gpu-17 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: R0001: page fault, client 0x1: read, address 0x00000000
Mar 15 09:12:34 host-gpu-17 kernel: NVRM: GPU Memory Region mapping failed: mmap failed (12)
Mar 15 09:12:35 host-gpu-17 kernel: oom-killer invoked for pid 7890 (python)```
Darren L.: hmm mmap failed (12) = ENOMEM from kernel, could be sysctl overcommit or kernel memory fragmentation. can we check /proc/meminfo and any oom_score of that pid?
Maya P.: /proc/meminfo on that host shows low Committed_AS spike. I can repro locally with a reduced test that allocates pinned pages and fails when concurrency >= 6.
Sophie Z.: try setting vm.mmap_min_addr and vm.overcommit_memory tuning? also try running with `--num-workers=1` to see if it's purely concurrent allocation related.
Darren L.: I'm going to create a small reproducer harness that stresses pinned allocations and run on the same image. if repro, we can bisect between kvcache allocator change and driver bump.
Maya P.: thanks. if you can reproduce, add `rd_kv_cache=0` env to try disabling the new allocator quickly.
CI Bot: build 3163010055 started on host-gpu-22 (pinned MIG). logs: https://ci.internal/build/3163010055/logs
Raul M.: scheduling a canary run on host-gpu-09 with updated driver (535.103) and telemetry. will compare nvlink/peer topo before/after.
Sophie Z.: small checklist: 1) rerun pinned MIG (in flight) 2) reproduce locally with repro harness 3) try with rd_kv_cache=0 4) collect dmesg/kern.log + nvidia-smi topo -m 5) if repro, run bisect over runtime change (kvcache) vs image (cuda 12.4)
Maya P.: perfect. I'll monitor the rerun and attach any failing core dumps. tagging @Darren L. and @Sophie Z. for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
Darren L.: will update thread with reproducer link and bisect plan within 2 hours.
Maya P.: last note — dropping a small gdb snippet to capture faulting address if we hit it again: ```gdb attach <pid> -ex 'thread apply all bt full' -ex detach -ex quit```
CI Bot: build 3163010055 finished — no failures on pinned MIG run (green). Marking canary success but leaving test reruns for 10 more builds.
Maya P.: interesting — canary green suggests placement-sensitive. we'll proceed with reproducer + disable allocator test. will open a bisect PR if repro confirmed.
Sophie Z.: thanks all. ping here when you have the reproducer link or kernel logs.
Maya P.: will do.
